brief.headline: Dig deeper: the core traction numbers are unverified and the founder gave 40 customers live against 26 in the deck, so the $15M ask can't yet be underwritten.
brief.summary: LabLoop sells robotic sample-prep automation to contract labs. It is raising a $3M seed at $15M pre-money on a deck claiming 26 paying customers, $38k MRR and 40% month-on-month growth. The $5M year-3 forecast is consistent with the deck's own market maths, and the pitch is internally coherent. Nothing on traction, team or revenue could be verified; no public record of the company was found, and the only 'LabLoop' hit is an unrelated campus equipment-sharing project. The 'no direct competitors' claim is contradicted (Opentrons at about $16k-$25k, Hamilton and Tecan, plus iLab and Quartzy in booking), though that check is hedged on which product is meant. The valuation is 33x ARR, the growth rate implies about $1.3k MRR ten months ago, and $90k burn across 25 people is only $3.6k per head, so the numbers don't fit together.
strengths: Clear wedge: manual sample prep and pipetting rework in contract labs, with a price pitch against $100k-$500k+ incumbent liquid handlers.
Stated traction of $38k MRR (about $456k ARR) from 26 customers (about $1.5k per customer per month) is plausible for a seed company if documented.
The $5M year-3 forecast fits the deck's own TAM-times-share maths (about $82M at the targeted share).
Team story is relevant (Thermo Fisher operator CEO, robotics PhD CTO), though unverified.

red_flags.text: Customer count changed between deck (26 paying) and live pitch (40 paying), and the live figure may include pilots. The ask, MRR and growth all rest on this number, and no public source confirms either one.

The 40% monthly growth implies MRR of about $1.3k ten months ago (28.9x). If it continued for another 12 months, MRR would be about $2.2M. This is self-reported and unverified, and the cohort and customer-count history is needed to test it.
The $15M pre-money is 33x current ARR and 3.0x year-3 forecast revenue, so the valuation relies on unverified traction and an aggressive growth path.

'No direct competitors' is contradicted: Opentrons already sells robots at about $16k-$25k, Hamilton and Tecan own the high end, and iLab and Quartzy are entrenched in equipment booking. The founder repeated 'nobody else is doing what we do' live, and the 10x price advantage is unverified.

The financials don't reconcile: $90k monthly burn across 25 people is $3.6k per head, below typical loaded salaries. Either headcount or burn is off, and the 33-month runway depends on the burn figure.

questions: You said 40 paying customers live but the deck says 26. Which is current, how many are paying versus on pilots, and what is MRR per customer?
Walk us through monthly MRR and customer count by cohort since January. How does 40% monthly growth, from about $1.3k MRR ten months ago, get to $38k, and how does it get to $5M in year 3?
Who do customers evaluate you against (Opentrons, Hamilton, Tecan, others), and why did your last 10 wins choose you? What is your actual price versus theirs?
Your $90k burn across 25 people is $3.6k per head. Who is on payroll, full-time or part-time, and what does $3M fund beyond the 33 months of current burn?
How did you build the $4.1B TAM, and which of the founders actually worked at Thermo Fisher, in what roles and for how long?
